ui_location: Talus > Hawkins Classification > Type I Nondisplaced
web_text_verbatim: Hawkins Type I: Nondisplaced vertical talar neck fracture; subtalar, ankle, and talonavicular joints remain anatomically aligned and congruous; low risk of AVN (<5-10%).
focus: Talus - Hawkins Type I nondisplaced criteria

quote: Type I fractures are considered nondisplaced, without associated incongruence of the subtalar, ankle, or talonavicular joint.

ui_location: Talus > Hawkins Classification > Type II Subtalar Dislocation
web_text_verbatim: Hawkins Type II: Displaced talar neck fracture with subtalar joint subluxation or dislocation; ankle (tibiotalar) joint remains anatomically congruous; AVN risk 20-50%.
focus: Talus - Hawkins Type II subtalar subluxation/dislocation
suggested_fix: None needed. Confirmed in Rockwood 10th ed.
quote: Hawkins type II injuries involve a fracture of the talar neck with any associated subtalar subluxation or dislocation. The relationship of the talus with respect to the ankle mortise and navicular is preserved in these injuries.

ui_location: Talus > Hawkins Classification > Type III Dislocation
web_text_verbatim: Hawkins Type III: Displaced talar neck fracture with dislocation of both subtalar and tibiotalar (ankle) joints; high rate of AVN (80-100%).

quote: Hawkins type III injuries involve a fracture through the talar neck with an associated talar body dislocation, which has been extruded, either partially or completely, from both the ankle and subtalar joints.

ui_location: 5th Metatarsal Base > Clinical Concept > Zone 1 Conservative Care
